ai.description: The leopard gecko reaches 18–25 cm. It features a yellow body with dark spots, a thick, fleshy tail, and moveable eyelids. Its skin has a bumpy, granular texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the presence of movable eyelids, which distinguishes *Eublepharis macularius* from all other Indian gecko families that possess fixed, transparent spectacles.
ai.habitat: Leopard geckos inhabit arid, rocky grasslands and dry scrublands across the Indian subcontinent, typically found at elevations ranging from sea level to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Leopard geckos are primarily crepuscular, meaning they are most active during the twilight hours of dawn and dusk to hunt insects while avoiding extreme temperatures.
ai.reproductionNotes: Leopard geckos are oviparous, typically laying two eggs per clutch. In India, they breed seasonally from early spring to late summer, often producing multiple clutches.
ai.distributionRemarks: The leopard gecko inhabits arid regions of northwestern India, primarily across Rajasthan and parts of Gujarat, typically at low to moderate elevations.
